## What to look for

- Which country lost the most people? Which lost the largest share of its population? Why is it not the same country?
- How wide is the range of the estimates for the Soviet Union, in millions? Why might the estimates differ so much?
- Compare the shares of France, the United Kingdom and the United States with those of Poland, Yugoslavia and the Soviet Union: what do you notice?
- How many Swiss dead are counted? Why so few?

## How it works

Each country has a low and a high estimate of its dead, soldiers and civilians together; the bar stands at the middle of the two. The share divides these figures by the population of the country on 1 January 1939. The Soviet Union is counted within its borders of 1946–1991, Poland within its borders of 1939, and China from 1937 to 1945. Only eleven countries are shown.
